meta.description: Grace Hopper really did say this — but her documented 1976 wording was "a DP manager… that way." The popular version is a later paraphrase.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: 1906–1992 · U.S. Navy Rear Admiral & pioneering computer scientist
answer.sourceLine: Grace Hopper really did press this idea — the earliest strong match is a 1976 Computerworld interview where she called “We’ve always done it that way” the most dangerous phrase a data-processing manager can use. But the tidy popular version (“the most dangerous phrase in the language … this way”) is a later smoothing, not wording pinned to any single primary source.

source.excerpt: “… the most dangerous phrase a DP manager can use is ‘We’ve always done it that way.’”
trail: Quote Investigator traces the earliest strong match to a 1976 Computerworld interview and notes Hopper voiced the idea more than once with shifting wording (“dangerous,” later “damaging”) — read the investigation.

A 1975 Baltimore Sun profile shows Hopper already using the theme without the word “dangerous,” warning how hard it is to change minds that say “But we’ve always done it this way” — per QI’s chronology.
Wikiquote lists the polished form in its Disputed section, pointing to Quote Investigator rather than to any primary Hopper source for the exact wording.
source.cutTag: Documented 1976; popular wording is a paraphrase

author.heading: About Grace Hopper
author.metaLine: 1906–1992 · U.S. Navy Rear Admiral & computer-science pioneer
author.bio: Grace Murray Hopper was an American mathematician and U.S. Navy officer who helped build the earliest computers and championed machine-independent programming, work that led to COBOL. A relentless advocate for questioning inherited habits, she gave countless talks warning organizations against complacency — making this line squarely consistent with her documented views.

misattribution.heading: Genuine idea, polished wording
misattribution.intro: This is not a fabrication pinned on a famous name — Grace Hopper really did make this point, repeatedly. What circulates online is a cleaned-up version of her documented words.

items.why: Her earliest strong documented line was “the most dangerous phrase a DP manager can use is ‘We’ve always done it that way’” (Computerworld, 1976). The popular “in the language … this way” form drops the data-processing context and smooths the phrasing — per Quote Investigator.
Hopper voiced the notion more than once with different words — a 1987 citation uses “damaging” rather than “dangerous,” showing there is no single fixed original sentence to quote, as QI documents.

misattribution.truthLine: The credit to Grace Hopper is sound; the exact popular sentence is a later paraphrase of her documented 1976 remark, not a verbatim quotation.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Grace Hopper spent decades urging engineers and managers to stop deferring to habit, so a line about the danger of “we’ve always done it this way” fits her thinking exactly. The question is only whether the crisp sentence people share is her literal wording — and the record shows it is a tidied version rather than a verbatim quote.
context.pull: The idea is authentically Hopper’s; the polished sentence is the internet’s.
